title: Education workers hold slow-drive protest in Madrid

tea.why: Education workers protest as part of an ongoing indefinite strike for public education.
tea.want: Defend public education and support the indefinite strike.
tea.changed: Nov 24: Teachers conducted slow-drive and bicycle protests from multiple points toward central Madrid during morning rush hour.

summary: Education workers participating in an indefinite strike across non-university education carried out slow-drive and bicycle protests entering central Madrid during morning rush hour. Organised by education unions, the action involved eight car columns from various locations around the region and four bicycle routes inside the capital, driving at low speeds to highlight their ongoing demands. The municipal government and traffic authorities reported increased congestion on major access routes and the M-30, though they noted it was difficult to isolate the protest's specific impact from regular heavy traffic. The regional transport minister criticised the action for potentially endangering traffic safety and inconveniencing local citizens, while union representatives deemed the demonstration a success.
response: Municipal and DGT authorities noted heavier traffic and increased congestion during the morning rush hour, though they stated it was difficult to isolate the protest from normal delays. The regional transport minister criticised the action for risking traffic safety and inconveniencing residents, according to El País.

updates.text: An indefinite strike in non-university education began.
Teachers carried out slow-drive car and bicycle protests converging on central Madrid during morning rush hour.
